title: MVR: Multi-view Video Reward Shaping for Reinforcement Learning
claim: Videos from multiple viewpoints are scored by a frozen VLM to produce visual guidance that shapes the agent's reward.
layout: Single panel, loop: environment → multi-camera videos → VLM → MVR → environment
description: A single closed-loop diagram. At left, a smiling globe icon stands for the environment. A dashed circular arrow connects it to a small humanoid robot in the middle, representing the agent acting in the environment. Three camera icons at different angles point at three rounded rows. Each row holds five silhouette frames of the humanoid running, so each row is one viewpoint's video. A gray arrow runs from the video stack down to a colorful circuit-brain icon labeled VLM. From there an arrow leads left to a box labeled MVR. A final arrow rises from MVR to the globe, labeled Visual Guidance. A small bar chart with a downward trend arrow at bottom left hints at the guidance fading over time. The eye goes first to the stacked robot frames at the right.
caption: The proposed MVR computes visual guidance using a VLM and videos collected from multiple viewpoints. In this example, the task requires a humanoid robot to run forward. Being captured from different viewpoints, the image sequences encode complementary information and enable comprehensive evaluation of the agent's behaviors. This example also illustrates the pitfall of using image-text similarity for dynamic tasks—running requires rhythmic alternation of legs, but optimizing image-text similarity leads to realizing the pose that best matches "running" repeatedly. The shaping term prioritizes states that establish alternating leg cadence; once a stable gait and the target forward speed are achieved, its influence automatically decreases and the task reward takes precedence (see [ref]).
abstract: Reward design is of great importance for solving complex tasks with reinforcement learning. Recent studies have explored using image-text similarity produced by vision-language models (VLMs) to augment rewards of a task with visual feedback. A common practice linearly adds VLM scores to task or success rewards without explicit shaping, potentially altering the optimal policy. Moreover, such approaches, often relying on single static images, struggle with tasks whose desired behavior involves complex, dynamic motions spanning multiple visually different states. Furthermore, single viewpoints can occlude critical aspects of an agent's behavior. To address these issues, this paper presents Multi-View Video Reward Shaping (MVR), a framework that models the relevance of states regarding the target task using videos captured from multiple viewpoints. MVR leverages video-text similarity from a frozen pre-trained VLM to learn a state relevance function that mitigates the bias towards specific static poses inherent in image-based methods. Additionally, we introduce a state-dependent reward shaping formulation that integrates task-specific rewards and VLM-based guidance, automatically reducing the influence of VLM guidance once the desired motion pattern is achieved. We confirm the efficacy of the proposed framework with extensive experiments on challenging humanoid locomotion tasks from HumanoidBench and manipulation tasks from MetaWorld, verifying the design choices through ablation studies.
